intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: A multi-day guided trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes. Stay in teahouses along the route for an authentic experience. Begin trekking from Day 2 to maximize the 14-day window. Choose a starting lodge in Nayapul or Tikhedhunga to avoid long travel from Pokhara on arrival day.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: A rewarding short hike to Poon Hill at 3,210m for panoramic sunrise views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Machhapuchhre peaks. Depart at 4:30 AM from Ghorepani for the best golden-hour light. Stay overnight in Ghorepani to be positioned right at the trailhead, eliminating long morning travel.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: A less-crowded alternative trek leading to Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500m through dense forests and alpine meadows with stunning close-up views of the Annapurna massif. Ideal for days 8–11 of the itinerary. Base yourself in Landruk village, which sits directly on the trail, cutting out unnecessary transit time.
experiences.location: Landruk to Mardi Himal Base Camp, Eastern Annapurna

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk and Nature Immersion
experiences.description: A guided half-day nature and cultural walk through traditional Gurung villages such as Ghandruk, exploring local flora, fauna, and community life. Learn about medicinal plants, bird species, and Gurung customs. Ghandruk is a central hub well-connected to multiple trek routes, making it an ideal base to avoid wasted travel time.

experiences.name: Birethanti to Tikhedhunga Riverside Trail Hike
experiences.description: A scenic introductory hike along the Modi Khola river from Birethanti to Tikhedhunga, ideal for Day 2 after a late Day 1 arrival. This gentle trail eases trekkers into the Annapurna circuit with lush subtropical scenery, waterfalls, and suspension bridges. Staying overnight in Birethanti means you can start hiking immediately after breakfast without any vehicle transfers.
experiences.location: Birethanti to Tikhedhunga, Lower Modi Khola Valley

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival — no activities scheduled before 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and exchange currency at the airport (rates are reasonable). Take a local bus or shared taxi to Thamel (budget ~$3–5 USD). Check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk around Thamel to get oriented — browse trekking gear shops for any last-minute supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's vibrant streets. Visit the nearby Kathmandu Durbar Square for a quick evening glimpse (entry ~$3 for SAARC, ~$15 for others — optional on Day 1). Relax and rest early to prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel restaurant (~$3–4 USD) such as OR2K or a local teahouse
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at a local Nepali restaurant in Thamel — try thukpa (noodle soup) or momos (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Carry some USD for initial expenses. Avoid touts at the airport. Book your Pokhara bus/jeep ticket tonight for an early departure tomorrow. Rest well — acclimatization starts now.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00 AM). Grab a quick breakfast near the bus park. Take the tourist bus or local bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara (departs ~7:00–8:00 AM, ~$8–12 USD tourist bus, ~$5 local bus, 6–7 hours). Enjoy scenic mountain and river valley views along the Prithvi Highway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 2:00–3:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse in Lakeside (Baidam area) — expect to pay ~$8–15/night for a clean room. Drop your bags and walk to Phewa Lake. Rent a rowboat (~$5/hour) or simply stroll along the lakeside promenade enjoying views of the Annapurna range.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake with the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks glowing in the alpenglow. Visit the Lakeside market for budget shopping — trekking gear, snacks, and supplies. Finalize your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS card plan for tomorrow morning.

meals.breakfast: Bread, eggs, and tea at a Thamel bakery (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from Thamel or eat at a roadside dhaba along the Kathmandu–Pokhara highway (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at a Lakeside budget restaurant (~$3–5 USD) — try Moondance or a local teahouse

day_by_day.notes: Book the tourist bus the night before for comfort. Confirm ACAP permit requirements — you'll need your passport photos and USD/NPR cash. The ACAP permit costs ~$30 USD and TIMS card ~$20 USD. Obtain these at the Tourism Board office in Pokhara (Damside) first thing tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning (7:00 AM): Visit the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara (Damside) to obtain your ACAP permit (~$30 USD) and TIMS card (~$20 USD) — bring 2 passport photos and your passport. Return to Lakeside, pack your trekking bag, and take a local taxi or jeep to Nayapul (~$10–15 for a shared jeep, 1.5 hours). Begin trekking from Nayapul toward Tikhedhunga (1,540m) — a gentle 2–3 hour walk through terraced fields and small villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga, crossing the Modi Khola river and ascending the famous stone staircase toward Ulleri (1,960m). This steep 45-minute climb is challenging but rewarding. Continue to Ghorepani (2,860m) if energy allows, or rest at Ulleri teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ghorepani and check into Ghorepani Boutique Stay. Settle in, dry your gear, and warm up with ginger lemon honey tea. Enjoy the spectacular sunset views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South from Ghorepani ridge. Chat with fellow trekkers and plan the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with toast at Lakeside guesthouse (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a Tikhedhunga teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Ghorepani Boutique Stay teahouse (~$5–7 USD) — hearty and unlimited refills

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance today: ~14–16 km, 5–7 hours. Start early to avoid afternoon clouds. Carry at least 2 liters of water. Wear layers — Ghorepani gets cold at night (October temperatures can drop to 5–8°C). Set your alarm for 4:30 AM for Poon Hill sunrise tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn (4:30 AM): Wake up and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — a 45-minute steep climb in the dark with a headlamp. Witness one of the most iconic sunrises in the Himalayas: Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre all bathed in golden light. Entry fee ~$2 USD. Spend 1–1.5 hours at the top photographing and soaking in the panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a late breakfast. Rest at the lodge and explore the rhododendron forests around Ghorepani village. These forests are spectacular in spring but still beautiful in October with changing leaves. Visit the small local village, interact with Magar community members, and explore the local market.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Ghorepani Boutique Stay. Enjoy a warm cup of masala tea on the lodge terrace with mountain views. Write in your journal, review photos, and plan the next day's trek toward Tadapani. Early bedtime (8:30–9:00 PM) to recover energy.

meals.breakfast: Bring hot tea/coffee in a thermos to Poon Hill; proper breakfast (pancakes or porridge) at the lodge after descent (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or noodle soup at the lodge (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with lentil soup and seasonal vegetables at Ghorepani Boutique Stay (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the Annapurna Circuit/Ghorepani loop — don't miss it! Dress in warm layers for the pre-dawn hike (temperature at the top can be near 0°C in October). Carry your headlamp and trekking poles. The viewpoint can get crowded — arrive slightly early for the best spots.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast (7:00 AM), begin trekking from Ghorepani toward Tadapani (2,630m) via the rhododendron and oak forest trail. This is a beautiful, moderately challenging trail (~4–5 hours, 10 km) passing through dense forest with occasional mountain views. Pass through Deurali (3,100m) — the highest point of today's route — and descend through forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tadapani by early afternoon. Check into a budget teahouse (~$5–8/night). Explore the small settlement and enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre from the village viewpoint. Rest your legs and take short walks on the surrounding trails.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the evening alpenglow on the Annapurna range from Tadapani's ridge. Tadapani offers some of the best unobstructed Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) views on the entire circuit. Socialize with other trekkers at the teahouse common room. Early rest.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and nuts at Ghorepani Boutique Stay (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the lodge or eat at Deurali teahouse — noodle soup or fried rice (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Tadapani teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. The Ghorepani–Tadapani trail is less crowded than the main circuit and offers pristine forest scenery. Watch for Himalayan monals (colorful pheasants) and langur monkeys in the rhododendron forest. Carry rain gear — October afternoons can bring brief showers.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (7:00 AM) from Tadapani, trekking down through dense rhododendron and bamboo forest toward Chomrong (2,170m) — a large Gurung village and gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. The trail descends steeply (~3 hours, 8 km). Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli growing larger as you approach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong by midday. Explore this beautiful Gurung village — visit the local monastery, interact with villagers, and enjoy sweeping views of the Annapurna massif and Modi Khola valley. Chomrong is a great place to rest. Take an optional short walk to the upper part of the village for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from Chomrong is spectacular — the entire Annapurna South face turns orange and pink. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the teahouse. This is a good night to treat yourself to a hot shower (usually available for ~$2–3 extra at teahouses). Chat with other trekkers about trail conditions ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eggs on toast or muesli at Tadapani teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a Chomrong teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or garlic soup with bread at Chomrong teahouse (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: ~8 km, 3–4 hours (mostly downhill). Chomrong is the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary — stock up on snacks, chocolate, and water purification tablets here (prices increase significantly higher up). There is a ACAP checkpoint in Chomrong — have your permit ready.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Chomrong. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a morning hike to the Chomrong viewpoint above the village for 360-degree views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, and the Modi Khola valley below. Visit the Chomrong monastery for a peaceful cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the terraced agricultural fields around Chomrong — October is harvest season, and you may see locals harvesting millet and corn. Visit the local school and small shops. Spend time journaling, reading, or simply sitting on a teahouse terrace watching the mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening. This is a great opportunity to do laundry (hand wash and air dry). Prepare your gear for the next stretch of trekking. Review your ACAP permit and plan the route for the coming days. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and butter at the teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Vegetable curry with rice at a local Chomrong restaurant (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat — go for a second helping (free refills!) at the teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are important for acclimatization and muscle recovery. Use this day to check your boots and gear for any issues. October in Chomrong is generally clear in the morning with possible afternoon clouds. Altitude here is 2,170m — you should feel well acclimatized before pushing higher.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (6:30 AM). Trek from Chomrong down the stone staircase, cross the Chomrong Khola river, and begin the ascent toward Sinuwa (2,360m) through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest. Continue past Kuldihar to Bamboo (2,310m) — a small teahouse cluster in a bamboo forest. Total: ~4 hours, 10 km.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate surroundings of Himalaya Hotel teahouse area. The gorge is stunning — massive walls of rock tower above you, and the roar of the Modi Khola river fills the air. Short walks along the gorge trail are rewarding.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner and early rest at Himalaya Hotel teahouse. The gorge gets dark early as the sun sets behind the towering ridges. This is a remote, atmospheric spot — enjoy the wilderness feeling. Temperature drops significantly at night.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs at Chomrong teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Bamboo teahouse (~$5–6 USD — prices increase in the sanctuary)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: ~12–14 km, 5–6 hours. The trail through the gorge can be slippery after rain — use trekking poles. Watch for avalanche zones (marked on the trail). Prices increase significantly inside the Annapurna Sanctuary — budget accordingly. Carry plenty of snacks and water purification tablets.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (6:30 AM). Trek from Himalaya Hotel through the narrowing gorge, passing Hinku Cave (a natural rock overhang used as shelter) and Deurali (3,230m). This section passes through potential avalanche zones — move quickly and stay alert. The gorge opens dramatically as you enter the Annapurna Sanctuary (also called Annapurna Base Camp area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Emerge from the gorge into the vast glacial amphitheater of the Annapurna Sanctuary. The landscape transforms dramatically — towering peaks surround you on all sides. Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m). Rest and acclimatize. The views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) from here are absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at MBC is otherworldly — the towering peaks of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre glow in shades of orange and pink. Wrap up warm (temperatures drop to -5°C or below at night) and enjoy the most spectacular mountain scenery of the entire trip. Early rest — altitude may cause mild headaches.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with dried fruit at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$4 USD)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (great for altitude) and bread at Deurali teahouse (~$6–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse (~$8–10 USD — highest prices on the route)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: ~10 km, 4–5 hours. Altitude gain is significant today — watch for symptoms of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS): headache, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite. Drink plenty of water (3+ liters/day). Eat garlic soup — locals swear by it for altitude. Do NOT push to ABC today if feeling unwell. Acclimatize at MBC first.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (5:00 AM) to catch sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m). The 1.5-hour hike from MBC to ABC in the pre-dawn darkness is magical — the stars above the sanctuary are incredibly bright. Arrive at ABC for sunrise: Annapurna I (8,091m), the 10th highest mountain in the world, towers directly above you. This is the highlight of the entire trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning exploring ABC — walk around the glacier moraine, visit the memorial chortens for mountaineers who lost their lives on Annapurna, and soak in the 360-degree panorama of some of the world's highest peaks. Begin descent back toward Bamboo or Dovan in the afternoon to aid acclimatization.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo or Dovan teahouse (lower altitude = better sleep). The descent from ABC to Bamboo takes approximately 4–5 hours. Celebrate your achievement at ABC with a hot meal and well-deserved rest. Your legs will feel the descent but your spirit will be soaring.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at MBC before dawn hike; proper breakfast (porridge/eggs) at ABC teahouse after sunrise (~$5–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at ABC or on the trail down (~$7–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Bamboo/Dovan teahouse (~$6–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m — this is the highest point of your trek. If you feel any serious AMS symptoms, descend immediately — altitude sickness can be life-threatening. October weather at ABC is generally clear in the morning. The descent from ABC to Bamboo in one day is long (5–6 hours) but recommended for acclimatization. Trekking poles essential for descent.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast (7:00 AM), continue descending from Bamboo/Dovan through the gorge, past Sinuwa, and back up to Chomrong (2,170m). The familiar trail feels different on the way back — you'll notice details you missed on the ascent. The ascent back up to Chomrong from the river crossing is steep but manageable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong by early afternoon. Rest, do laundry, and treat yourself to a hot shower. Visit the Chomrong bakery (famous among trekkers) for apple pie or cinnamon rolls — a well-deserved treat. Reflect on the incredible journey to ABC.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Chomrong with mountain views. This is your last night in the high mountains — savor the views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. Prepare your gear for the descent to lower elevations tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Porridge at Bamboo/Dovan teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Fried rice or noodle soup on the trail (~$5–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra helpings at Chomrong teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Trekking distance: ~12 km, 5–6 hours (mix of descent and ascent). Your knees will feel the descent — trekking poles and slow, steady steps protect your joints. Chomrong teahouses are a welcome return to relative comfort after the high-altitude teahouses. Stock up on water and snacks for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (7:00 AM). Trek from Chomrong down to the Modi Khola valley and take the trail toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m) — a small village famous for its natural hot springs on the riverbank. The hike takes approximately 2–3 hours through beautiful terraced fields and rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Jhinu Danda and descend to the natural hot springs on the Modi Khola riverbank (~15-minute walk from the village). Soak your tired legs and muscles in the natural thermal pools (~$3–5 entry fee) while listening to the roar of the river and looking up at the surrounding forested hills. This is one of the best rewards after a long trek.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jhinu Danda teahouse for the night. Alternatively, continue trekking 2–3 more hours to Nayapul if you want to save a day. Relax, enjoy the peaceful riverside setting, and celebrate the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary trek. The sense of achievement is immense.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Chomrong teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or dal bhat at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or vegetable curry at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are a trekker's paradise — don't miss them! The pools are best enjoyed in the late morning or early afternoon before they get crowded. Bring a towel and change of clothes. Trekking distance today: ~8–10 km, 3–4 hours. A relatively easy and rewarding day.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, trek from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (1,070m) — approximately 3–4 hours through villages, terraced fields, and along the Modi Khola river. The trail gradually descends through the lower Annapurna foothills with beautiful rural scenery. Arrive at Nayapul and take a local jeep or bus back to Pokhara (~1.5 hours, ~$3–5 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check back into a Lakeside guesthouse (~$8–15/night). Take a long, hot shower — your first proper shower in many days! Visit a local pharmacy if needed for any minor ailments. Rent a bicycle (~$3–5/day) or walk along the Phewa Lake promenade. Visit the International Mountain Museum (~$5 entry) to learn about Himalayan mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your Annapurna trek with a lakeside dinner. Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake with the Annapurna range glowing in the background — a perfect bookend to your trekking adventure. Browse the Lakeside market for souvenirs: Thangka paintings, prayer flags, pashmina scarves, and handmade crafts.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Snack on the trail or eat at a Nayapul roadside dhaba (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer lakeside restaurant — try Nepali set meal or pizza (~$6–10 USD) — you've earned it!

day_by_day.notes: You've completed an incredible trek! Total trekking distance over the journey: approximately 100–120 km. Take time to appreciate the achievement. Book your Kathmandu bus/flight ticket for tomorrow. Pokhara to Kathmandu: tourist bus (~$10–12), local bus (~$5), or domestic flight (~$80–100 USD if budget allows for the scenic flight).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise over Phewa Lake with the Annapurna range. Take a short rowboat ride on the lake at dawn (~$5 for 1 hour) — the reflections of the mountains on the still morning water are magical. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of Phewa Lake (rowboat included in lake entry). Pack your bags and check out of the guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tourist bus or local bus back to Kathmandu (departs ~7:00–8:00 AM, arrives ~2:00–3:00 PM). If time permits upon arrival in Kathmandu, visit Pashupatinath Temple (Hindu sacred site, free to walk the ghats area) or Boudhanath Stupa (~$3 entry) — one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world. Both are close to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Kathmandu. Visit Thamel for last-minute souvenir shopping — fixed-price shops are more reliable than haggling stalls. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Thamel. Reflect on 14 incredible days in the Annapurna region — the mountains, the trails, the people, and the culture. Pack your bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café breakfast — granola, yogurt, and fresh juice (~$4–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba meal along the Pokhara–Kathmandu highway (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Thamel rooftop restaurant — try Nepali thali or butter chicken (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight departs on Day 15 or later, use the extra time to explore Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, and Patan Durbar Square. Kathmandu Valley day tours cost ~$5–10 USD by local bus. Keep some NPR for last-minute expenses and airport taxes. Total estimated budget for 14 days (excluding flights): $400–600 USD for a budget-conscious traveler.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — clear immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a taxi to Pokhara (approximately 6–7 hours by road) or catch a short domestic flight to Pokhara (25 minutes). Check in to a mid-range lakeside hotel in Pokhara to rest and freshen up before the trek begins
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade in Pokhara, enjoy the mountain reflections at dusk, and explore the Lakeside Bazaar for trekking supplies or last-minute gear

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or a quick snack at Kathmandu airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at a roadside dhaba or airport café during transit
meals.dinner: Momos and dal bhat at a popular Lakeside restaurant such as OR2K or Caffe Concerto — budget NPR 800–1200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency at the airport or Lakhmandu ATMs. Confirm trekking permits (TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) — you can arrange these in Pokhara the next morning. Rest well as acclimatization begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Obtain TIMS card and ACAP permit at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara (Damside area). Hire a porter or guide if desired. Drive by jeep or taxi from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours), the official trek starting point
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin trekking from Nayapul (1,070m) through lush subtropical forest and terraced rice paddies to Tikhedhunga (1,540m), approximately 3–4 hours of moderate walking along the Modi Khola river valley
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga, check in to a mid-range teahouse, rest tired legs, and enjoy panoramic views of the foothills as the sun sets

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and tea at your Pokhara hotel — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Birethanti — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and lentil soup (dal bhat) at your Tikhedhunga teahouse — NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Tikhedhunga marks the foot of the famous 3,600-step stone staircase to Ulleri. Drink plenty of water and apply sunscreen. Teahouse accommodation in Tikhedhunga costs approximately NPR 300–600 per night (room often discounted if you dine there).

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the steep stone-staircase ascent from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri (2,010m) — approximately 1.5 hours of challenging uphill climbing with rewarding valley views. Continue through rhododendron and oak forest to Banthanti
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Banthanti (2,250m) through dense forest to Nangethanti and onward to Ghorepani (2,860m) — approximately 3–4 hours total from Ulleri. Check in to Ghorepani Boutique Stay and settle into your booked accommodation
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village of Ghorepani, browse small local shops, and enjoy a warm cup of ginger-lemon-honey tea on the teahouse terrace while watching alpenglow on Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and banana pancakes at Tikhedhunga teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and pasta or noodles at a Banthanti teahouse — NPR 400–700
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,860m — mild altitude effects possible. Hydrate well and avoid alcohol tonight. Ghorepani Boutique Stay typically offers comfortable rooms with attached or shared bathrooms; confirm your booking details on arrival. Set an alarm for 04:30 tomorrow for Poon Hill sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike (04:30–05:00 departure) to Poon Hill (3,210m) — a 45-minute uphill walk in the dark with headlamps. Witness one of Nepal's most iconic sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges including Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Nilgiri
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a late breakfast, then trek to Tadapani (2,630m) through pristine rhododendron forest (one of the largest rhododendron forests in the world) — approximately 3–4 hours of moderate trekking with excellent mountain views
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani, check in to a mid-range teahouse, and enjoy sweeping sunset views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak) and Annapurna South from the ridge-top village

meals.breakfast: Hot tea or coffee at Poon Hill viewpoint stall, then full breakfast back at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — NPR 400–700
meals.lunch: Tibetan bread with jam and honey or vegetable fried rice at a Deurali teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Pasta or pizza (teahouse-style) and hot chocolate at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Bring warm layers and a headlamp for the Poon Hill hike — temperatures can drop to 0–5°C before sunrise in October. The rhododendron forest between Ghorepani and Tadapani is spectacular even outside bloom season (peak bloom: March–April). October offers clear skies and excellent mountain visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning nature walk around Tadapani ridge for bird watching — the area hosts Himalayan pheasants, laughing thrushes, and various raptors. Trek from Tadapani down through forest to Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours with significant descent and some ascent
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong, a large and picturesque Gurung village with excellent views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Explore the village terraces, visit a local Gurung home if invited, and rest at your teahouse
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant teahouse atmosphere in Chhomrong — one of the last major villages before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Watch the sunset paint Annapurna South golden from the village viewpoint

meals.breakfast: Muesli with milk and eggs at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a mid-route teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Grilled yak cheese sandwich or vegetable curry with rice at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is a key junction village. Teahouses here are well-equipped with hot showers (NPR 200–300 extra). This is a good place to charge electronics and stock up on snacks for higher altitude days ahead. The stone-paved trail in Chhomrong is steep but well-maintained.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down stone steps to Sinuwa (2,360m) and continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Dovan (2,600m) — approximately 3–4 hours. The trail follows the Modi Khola gorge with dramatic canyon scenery
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Dovan through increasingly dramatic alpine terrain to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) — approximately 2 hours. The landscape becomes more rugged and the valley narrows impressively as you approach the Sanctuary gateway
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Himalaya Hotel teahouse, one of the last comfortable stops before the high-altitude Sanctuary. Enjoy the dramatic gorge views and listen to the roaring Modi Khola river below

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and tea at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (excellent for altitude) and noodles at Sinuwa or Dovan teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra vegetables at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is highly recommended at altitude as it is believed to aid acclimatization. Watch for potential afternoon cloud buildup in the gorge — October is generally clear but the canyon can be misty. Avalanche risk exists on certain sections; follow your guide's advice and move quickly through exposed areas.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through the dramatic 'gateway' boulders of the Annapurna Sanctuary to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — approximately 3–4 hours through stunning high-alpine terrain with glacial moraines and the sacred Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) towering overhead
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and acclimatize at MBC for 1–2 hours, then continue the final push to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approximately 1.5–2 hours through a glacial amphitheater surrounded by eight peaks above 7,000m
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at ABC and experience the overwhelming 360-degree panorama of the Annapurna Sanctuary — Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Tent Peak, and Machhapuchhre all visible. Watch the alpenglow on the peaks at sunset

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Himalaya Hotel — NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at MBC teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at ABC teahouse — NPR 700–1000 (prices increase at higher altitude)

day_by_day.notes: ABC sits at 4,130m — altitude sickness is a real concern. Move slowly, drink 3–4 liters of water, and descend immediately if you experience severe headache, vomiting, or loss of coordination. October temperatures at ABC can drop to -10°C at night — ensure you have a warm sleeping bag (rated to -15°C) and thermal layers. This is the highlight of the entire trek.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at ABC for the magical sunrise over the Annapurna Sanctuary — arguably one of the most spectacular mountain sunrises on Earth. Photograph the golden light hitting Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, and the surrounding giants. Explore the base camp area and glacial terrain
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back to MBC (1 hour) and continue down to Deurali (3,230m) or Himalaya Hotel — approximately 3–4 hours total descent through the gorge
day_by_day.evening: Rest weary legs at Himalaya Hotel or Deurali teahouse, enjoy the warmer temperatures at lower altitude, and reflect on the ABC achievement over a well-earned hot meal

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at sunrise, then full breakfast at ABC teahouse — NPR 600–900
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at MBC or en route teahouse — NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dal bhat and vegetable curry at Himalaya Hotel — NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Descent is significantly faster than ascent but can be hard on knees — use trekking poles. The return journey retraces the route through the gorge. October mornings at ABC are crystal clear before clouds build around midday — the sunrise experience is typically outstanding this time of year.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel back through the bamboo forest to Sinuwa and up to Chhomrong — approximately 4–5 hours with significant ascent on the Chhomrong stone staircase. The familiar trail feels different on the return journey
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest in Chhomrong, take a hot shower, and explore any village areas you missed on the way up. Visit the local tea shop or interact with Gurung villagers
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a celebratory dinner in Chhomrong — you have completed the Annapurna Sanctuary trek. Relax on the teahouse terrace with views of Annapurna South

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Sinuwa teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner: pizza, apple pie, and hot chocolate at a Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 800–1200

day_by_day.notes: Apple pie and cinnamon rolls are surprisingly good at Chhomrong teahouses — a beloved trekker tradition. Rest well as tomorrow involves a longer descent to lower elevations. Consider tipping your guide and porter at this stage if satisfied with their service.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward Ghorepani via a different scenic route through Tadapani — approximately 4–5 hours through rhododendron and oak forest with continued Annapurna and Machhapuchhre views
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Ghorepani and check in to Ghorepani Boutique Stay for a second night. Use the afternoon for a relaxed walk around the village, visit local homes, and explore the small monastery near the village
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ghorepani Boutique Stay for a comfortable evening — enjoy the familiar surroundings and the satisfaction of a completed Annapurna Sanctuary circuit

meals.breakfast: Porridge and banana pancakes at Chhomrong teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and lentil soup at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Returning to Ghorepani Boutique Stay provides a comfortable mid-trek rest point. October evenings in Ghorepani are cool (5–10°C) — bring warm layers. Consider an optional second Poon Hill sunrise visit tomorrow morning if weather is clear.

day_by_day.morning: Optional second sunrise hike to Poon Hill (04:30 departure) for different lighting and photographic conditions, OR sleep in and take a gentle morning nature walk on the ridge trails around Ghorepani through the rhododendron forest
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani down to Tikhedhunga via Ulleri — descending the famous 3,600 stone steps (approximately 3–4 hours). The descent is steep but the views of the Modi Khola valley and terraced farmland are beautiful
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Birethanti (1,025m) or Nayapul and arrange transport back to Pokhara (1.5–2 hours by jeep or local bus). Check in to a Lakeside Pokhara hotel and enjoy your first hot shower in days

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — NPR 400–700
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at Ulleri teahouse — NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a Pokhara Lakeside restaurant — try Moondance Restaurant or Boomerang for excellent Nepali and international cuisine — NPR 1000–1500

day_by_day.notes: The knee-jarring descent from Ghorepani to Tikhedhunga is one of the most challenging sections — trekking poles are strongly recommended. Nayapul has regular jeep and bus connections to Pokhara. Arrive in Pokhara by early evening for maximum rest time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in, then take a peaceful rowboat ride on Phewa Lake (NPR 400–600 per hour) with reflections of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South on the water — a serene contrast to the high-altitude trek
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (NPR 400 entry) — an excellent museum documenting Himalayan mountaineering history, Nepali culture, and mountain ecosystems. Alternatively, visit the Devi's Fall waterfall and Gupteshwor Cave nearby
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pokhara's Lakeside market for handicrafts, trekking souvenirs, Thangka paintings, and pashmina shawls. Enjoy a relaxing lakeside dinner as the mountains glow at dusk

meals.breakfast: Full Western breakfast at your Pokhara hotel or a Lakeside café — NPR 500–800
meals.lunch: Newari set meal at a local restaurant or thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup) — NPR 500–800
meals.dinner: Grilled fish from Phewa Lake and local Pokhara specialties at Busy Bee Café or Caffe Concerto — NPR 900–1400

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is a perfect recovery destination with excellent food, comfortable accommodation, and stunning mountain views. Consider booking a yoga or massage session (NPR 1000–2000) to aid muscle recovery after 10 days of trekking. Laundry services are widely available at NPR 100–150 per kg.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise paragliding flight over Pokhara (NPR 8,000–12,000) from Sarangkot Hill for a bird's-eye view of the Annapurna range and Phewa Lake — one of the world's best paragliding destinations. Alternatively, hike up to Sarangkot viewpoint (1,592m) for panoramic mountain views (free, 1.5 hours uphill)
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the southern ridge of Phewa Lake — accessible by boat and a short hike (30 minutes) for 360-degree views of Pokhara valley, the lake, and the Annapurna range. Explore the Old Bazaar (Bagar area) of Pokhara for authentic local shopping
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — enjoy a sunset cruise on Phewa Lake (NPR 500–800) and then a farewell dinner at one of Pokhara's finest restaurants

meals.breakfast: Eggs Benedict or full breakfast at a Lakeside café — NPR 500–800
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a lakeside restaurant — mixed salad, soup, and juice — NPR 600–900
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Moondance Restaurant — Nepali set meal with raksi (local spirit) or tongba (millet beer) — NPR 1200–1800

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding in Pokhara is extremely safe with professional operators — book through reputable companies like Blue Sky Paragliding or Sunrise Paragliding. October offers excellent flying conditions with clear skies. The World Peace Pagoda is a beautiful and peaceful site worth visiting at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal — take a last peaceful walk along Phewa Lake promenade at sunrise for one final view of the Annapurna massif reflected in the lake. Pack, check out of hotel, and purchase any final souvenirs or gifts from Lakeside market
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Pokhara to Kathmandu by domestic flight (25 minutes, recommended) or tourist bus (7–8 hours). If flying, arrive in Kathmandu with time to visit Thamel neighborhood for last-minute shopping, or take a taxi to Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa for a final cultural experience
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Arrive at the airport 3 hours before international departure. Reflect on 14 extraordinary days in the Annapurna region of Nepal

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast — sel roti (ring-shaped rice bread) with yogurt and honey at a local Pokhara café — NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Pokhara airport or Kathmandu Thamel restaurant — NPR 500–800
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Domestic flights Pokhara–Kathmandu cost approximately USD 100–120 and are highly recommended over the long bus journey. Book in advance as October is peak season. Kathmandu airport security can be slow — arrive early. Ensure all trekking permits and receipts are kept as souvenirs. Nepal imposes a departure tax included in most international ticket prices.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your hotel in Thamel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at a premium heritage hotel in Kathmandu (e.g., Dwarika's Hotel or Hyatt Regency). Freshen up and take a leisurely guided walk through the UNESCO-listed Pashupatinath Temple complex and Boudhanath Stupa area to acclimatize and absorb the spiritual atmosphere of Kathmandu.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop cocktails overlooking the Kathmandu valley skyline. Attend a curated cultural Newari dance performance arranged by your concierge.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch at the hotel restaurant upon arrival — traditional Nepali thali with organic ingredients and locally sourced produce
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Krishnarpan Restaurant (Dwarika's Hotel) — a multi-course Newari tasting menu with rare heritage recipes paired with Himalayan herbal teas and premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passports and visa documentation are ready for immigration. A private airport greeter and luxury SUV transfer should be pre-arranged. Begin light hydration protocol to prepare for altitude in coming days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private guided tour of Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple) at sunrise for panoramic views of Kathmandu Valley. Followed by a heritage walking tour of Patan Durbar Square with an expert local historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter or scenic mountain flight briefing and preparation. Visit the Garden of Dreams for a peaceful afternoon stroll, then browse curated trekking gear and Himalayan handicrafts at premium outfitters in Thamel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Kathmandu dinner at Bhojan Griha — a restored Rana-era mansion serving authentic Nepali cuisine in a royal setting with live sarangi music.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the hotel — fresh Himalayan fruits, eggs to order, Tibetan bread, and organic Ilam tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a rooftop café in Patan — wood-fired Newari specialties and fresh-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Royal Nepali multi-course dinner at Bhojan Griha with premium imported wines and artisanal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Confirm helicopter or mountain flight booking for Day 3 if weather permits. Pack and organize trekking gear for the Annapurna journey beginning Day 3. Hydrate well and avoid alcohol in excess to prepare for altitude gain.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer or scenic flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara (45-minute flight recommended for premium experience). Arrive in Pokhara and check in at a lakeside luxury lodge (e.g., Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or Pavilions Himalayas). Morning at leisure with views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat excursion on Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna massif reflecting on the water. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the lake island. Afternoon hike to the World Peace Pagoda for sweeping panoramic views of the Himalayas and Pokhara valley.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the lodge terrace with unobstructed Himalayan panoramas. Curated stargazing session with a local astronomer guide.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or hotel breakfast — continental spread with Himalayan honey, fresh fruits, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside gourmet lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant — fresh trout from Phewa Lake, organic salads, and local craft beer
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner on the lodge terrace — chef's tasting menu featuring Gurung tribal recipes, Himalayan cheeses, and fine imported wines

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — expect clear skies and stunning mountain views. Confirm trekking permits (TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) are arranged by your tour operator. Begin final gear checks.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for sunrise views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) from the lodge. Post-sunrise yoga and meditation session led by a private instructor on the lodge lawn. Gourmet breakfast before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private vehicle transfer from Pokhara to Nayapul (approximately 1.5 hours). Begin the trek from Nayapul through terraced rice fields, rhododendron forests, and traditional Gurung villages toward Tikhedhunga or Ulleri (approximately 3–4 hours of moderate trekking). Arrive and check in at the best available teahouse-style lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Guided village walk through Ulleri to interact with local Gurung and Magar communities. Warm up by the lodge fire with Himalayan herbal tea and local raksi (rice wine).

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Pokhara lodge — eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, granola, and Himalayan tea selection
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the lodge chef — enjoyed at a scenic riverside stop en route
meals.dinner: Dal bhat tarkari (the classic Nepali trekker's meal) with freshly made pickles, seasonal vegetables, and unlimited refills at the best lodge in Ulleri

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 8–10 km with significant elevation gain (Ulleri sits at ~1,960m). Pace yourself and stay well hydrated. Your premium guide will carry emergency supplies and a first-aid kit.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek from Ulleri through dense rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (2,860m). The trail passes through Banthanti and Nangethanti — enjoy the dramatic forest scenery and possible wildlife sightings including Himalayan tahr and langur monkeys. Arrive Ghorepani by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — your premium accommodation for the next several nights. Settle in and explore the charming village of Ghorepani. Optional short acclimatization hike to the lower ridge for initial Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South views.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up in the boutique lodge lounge with a wood fire, premium Darjeeling tea, and freshly baked goods. Briefing by your guide on the Poon Hill sunrise trek for the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Hearty trekker's breakfast at the Ulleri lodge — porridge with dried fruits, Tibetan bread with honey, boiled eggs, and hot tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Banthanti teahouse — vegetable noodle soup, momos (dumplings), and fresh lemon tea
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — roasted seasonal vegetables, Himalayan herb soup, lentil curry, and homemade apple pie with cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,860m — take it easy this evening to acclimatize properly. Drink plenty of fluids, avoid alcohol, and retire early for the 4:30 AM Poon Hill wake-up call tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:30 AM for the iconic Poon Hill (3,210m) sunrise trek — approximately 45 minutes uphill. Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan panoramas on Earth: Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, and over a dozen other peaks bathed in golden alpenglow. Return to Ghorepani Boutique Stay for a full breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended guided nature hike along the Ghorepani ridge trail through pristine rhododendron forests — your guide will identify rare Himalayan flora and fauna. Visit the Magar and Gurung cultural museum in the village. Afternoon photography session from the ridge with a dedicated mountain photography guide.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the boutique stay — optional Himalayan hot stone massage or aromatherapy treatment. Fireside storytelling session with your guide about Annapurna's mountaineering history.

meals.breakfast: Post-Poon Hill celebration breakfast at the boutique stay — full hot breakfast spread with pancakes, eggs, fresh Himalayan honey, seasonal fruit, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch at the lodge — pumpkin soup, grilled cheese sandwich on homemade bread, and herbal infusion
meals.dinner: Special chef's dinner at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — slow-cooked Gurung lamb curry, sautéed wild mushrooms, steamed rice, and warm chocolate brownie with cream

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers for the Poon Hill sunrise — temperatures can drop to 0°C or below at 3,210m in October. Bring a headlamp, gloves, and a warm hat. The view is considered one of the finest in the entire Himalayas.

day_by_day.morning: Guided half-day trek from Ghorepani toward Tadapani through a stunning high-altitude rhododendron forest (world's largest rhododendron forest — spectacular even outside bloom season). The trail offers continuous close-up views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Arrive Tadapani (2,630m) by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tadapani village and the surrounding forest trails. Optional birdwatching session — October brings Himalayan monal pheasants, blood pheasants, and various raptors. Rest and acclimatize at the premium teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return trek to Ghorepani Boutique Stay (approximately 2 hours) through the forest at golden hour — magical light filtering through the rhododendron canopy. Arrive in time for sunset views from the lodge terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — French toast with Himalayan honey, muesli, seasonal fruits, and masala tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tadapani's best teahouse — dal bhat, seasonal vegetable curry, and hot lemon ginger tea
meals.dinner: Farm-to-table dinner at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — organic vegetable stew, grilled yak cheese, sourdough bread, and spiced Himalayan apple crumble

day_by_day.notes: The Ghorepani–Tadapani trail is moderately challenging with some steep sections. October foliage adds rich amber and gold tones to the forest. This is an excellent day for wildlife and bird photography.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and take a private guided meditation and breathing exercise session on the lodge terrace with Himalayan panoramas as your backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural immersion experience in Ghorepani village — visit a traditional Gurung household for a cooking demonstration and learn to prepare dal bhat, gundruk (fermented greens), and sel roti (rice doughnuts). Participate in weaving and traditional craft activities.
day_by_day.evening: Private bonfire evening at the boutique stay with curated Himalayan cocktails (hot toddy, raksi punch) and a special cultural performance by local Gurung musicians playing madal drums and bansuri flutes.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast — eggs any style, smoked cheese, fresh-baked Tibetan bread, granola parfait, and premium Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Participate in the Gurung cooking class and enjoy the meal you helped prepare — authentic dal bhat, gundruk pickle, and fresh yogurt
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — Himalayan trout (flown in from Pokhara), roasted root vegetables, herb-infused rice, and traditional kheer (rice pudding) with cardamom

day_by_day.notes: This is a planned rest and cultural immersion day — essential for acclimatization and rejuvenation mid-trek. Take time to journal, photograph, and absorb the extraordinary mountain environment around you.

day_by_day.morning: Second sunrise hike to Poon Hill — this time with a private photography guide and professional camera equipment rental available. The morning light at this time of year is exceptionally clear. Spend extended time on the summit capturing the full Annapurna and Dhaulagiri panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani down toward Chitre and Phalate, exploring lower elevation trails with views of terraced farmland and the Modi Khola valley below. Visit a traditional water mill and interact with local farmers harvesting autumn crops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ghorepani Boutique Stay for a relaxing evening. Optional private yoga session on the terrace. Review your photography from the trip with your guide over evening tea.

meals.breakfast: Post-sunrise breakfast at the boutique stay — warm porridge with dried berries, boiled eggs, fresh fruit plate, and ginger lemon honey tea
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail — gourmet packed box with sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — chef's special Nepali-fusion tasting menu with five courses, herbal digestif, and live acoustic guitar performance

day_by_day.notes: October 2027 is expected to offer exceptional visibility — the post-monsoon clarity typically provides the clearest mountain views of the year. A second visit to Poon Hill is highly recommended for photography enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Ghorepani on a full-day trek toward Chhomrong via the Kimrong Khola valley — a less-traveled premium route with extraordinary biodiversity and dramatic river gorge scenery. Trek through bamboo groves, oak forests, and terraced hillsides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Chhomrong village (2,170m) — a picturesque Gurung village with sweeping views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. Check in at the best available lodge. Explore the village and visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Chhomrong's famous viewpoint — Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) is particularly dramatic from this vantage point at dusk. Warm evening at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Ghorepani Boutique Stay — full hot spread with all favorites from the stay
meals.lunch: Trail-side lunch at a scenic teahouse in Kimrong — vegetable fried rice, hot soup, and fresh tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chhomrong's premium lodge — Gurung-style chicken curry, seasonal vegetables, steamed rice, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 5–6 hours with significant elevation change. The Kimrong route is less crowded than the main Annapurna Base Camp trail and offers a more intimate wilderness experience. Trekking poles highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Optional extension trek toward Sinuwa and the lower Annapurna Sanctuary trail for those wishing to experience the dramatic Modi Khola gorge and bamboo forest section. Alternatively, explore Chhomrong village in depth with a cultural guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return trek from Sinuwa to Chhomrong (or continue exploring the village). Rest at the lodge and enjoy the spectacular mountain views. Optional nature journaling or sketching session with a local artist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at Chhomrong's finest lodge — celebrate the high-altitude trekking experience with a premium meal and toasts to the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Hearty trekker's breakfast at Chhomrong lodge — porridge, Tibetan bread, fried eggs, and hot masala tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Sinuwa — dal bhat with unlimited refills and hot lemon tea
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Chhomrong lodge — slow-cooked buffalo stew, roasted potatoes, fresh salad, and homemade carrot cake with cream

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary — the atmosphere here is exceptional. October brings clear skies and the possibility of fresh snow on the high peaks above, creating stunning visual contrasts.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent trek from Chhomrong toward Jhinu Danda — famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola river. The trail descends through terraced fields and subtropical forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Jhinu Danda and soak in the natural hot springs — a deeply restorative experience after days of high-altitude trekking. The springs sit at the river's edge with views up toward the Annapurna peaks. Private hot spring session can be arranged for premium guests.
day_by_day.evening: Continue trekking or take a private vehicle from New Bridge to Nayapul, then luxury transfer back to Pokhara. Check in at your lakeside luxury lodge for the final nights in the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Chhomrong lodge — eggs, toast, honey, and fresh tea before the descent
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail near the Modi Khola river — gourmet packed box with sandwiches, fruits, and thermos of soup
meals.dinner: Welcome-back dinner at the Pokhara luxury lodge — international fusion menu, fresh Phewa Lake trout, premium wine selection, and indulgent dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a highlight of the Annapurna circuit — arrange a private session through your guide for an exclusive experience. The mineral-rich waters are renowned for soothing tired trekking muscles.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely sunrise from the Pokhara lakeside — optional sunrise kayak on Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna range reflecting on the water. Followed by a premium spa morning at the lodge — full body massage, steam bath, and facial treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Pokhara's highlights: the International Mountain Museum (world-class exhibits on Himalayan mountaineering history), Gupteshwor Cave, and Davis Falls. Afternoon shopping for premium Himalayan handicrafts, pashmina, and Thangka paintings at curated artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Pokhara dinner at a premium lakeside restaurant — rooftop dining with panoramic views of the illuminated Annapurna range under the stars. Live Nepali folk music performance.

meals.breakfast: Lavish breakfast at the lodge — full spread including fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant — wood-fired pizza, fresh salads, and artisan Nepali craft beer
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining at Pokhara's finest lakeside restaurant — multi-course tasting menu with Himalayan-inspired dishes, premium wine pairing, and live acoustic music

day_by_day.notes: This is a well-deserved rest and recovery day after the trekking. The spa treatment is highly recommended to rejuvenate before the final travel day. Confirm return flight details and Kathmandu transfer arrangements for Day 14.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise from Pokhara — last views of the Annapurna massif from the lakeside. Slow farewell breakfast at the lodge. Pack and prepare for departure. Optional final short walk along the lakeside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer or scenic flight back to Kathmandu. Depending on departure time, visit a final Kathmandu highlight — the Garden of Dreams or a curated shopping experience at premium Thamel boutiques for last-minute gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tribhuvan International Airport. Private luxury airport transfer with a dedicated farewell concierge. Carry unforgettable memories of the Annapurna Himalayas.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent breakfast at the Pokhara lodge — full hot and cold buffet with all favorites, freshly baked goods, and premium Nepali tea ceremony
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch in Kathmandu at a premium heritage restaurant — Newari cuisine tasting menu with traditional brass-served dishes
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge premium dining before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for Kathmandu airport check-in and security. Purchase any remaining souvenirs — pashmina, Himalayan tea, Thangka paintings, and handmade jewelry make excellent premium gifts. This 14-day journey covers Kathmandu, Pokhara, Ghorepani, Poon Hill, Tadapani, Chhomrong, and Jhinu Danda — a truly comprehensive and luxurious Annapurna experience.
